title: What is robotics, really?
description: A beginner-friendly map of how sensors, controllers, actuators and algorithms work together.
body:
A robot is more than a collection of motors and wires. It is a system that perceives information, processes it, and produces actions in the physical world.

The four building blocks

  1. Structure: the frame, wheels, gears, linkages and other mechanical parts.
  2. Sensors: devices that measure the environment or the robot's own state.
  3. Controller: a microcontroller or computer that runs the program.
  4. Actuators: motors, servos and other components that create motion.

From measurement to action

Imagine a wheeled robot following a dark line on a light floor. Its light sensors estimate where the line is. The program calculates the steering correction. Then the motors change speed to move the robot back towards the line.

A reliable robot is not defined by how many components it has, but by how well its parts work together.

Try it yourself

Draw a block diagram of a line-following robot. Mark each sensor, controller and actuator. Then answer: what happens if one sensor stops giving useful measurements?
